title: Two-Phase Stratified Pilot Discovery and Streaming Selective Feature Acquisition for Cost-Constrained Prediction
content: Predicting rare outcomes in hospital discharge planning, credit underwriting, fleet maintenance, and fraud screening frequently hits severe risk overlap on baseline covariates Xbase. Rather than resampling Xbase, resolving overlap under explicit budgets poses a two-stage design problem: (i) discovering non-redundant Stage-2 feature channels from a small two-phase pilot without measuring all M channels on 100% of training rows, and (ii) selectively querying discovered channels for arriving instances at deployment. First, we develop a constrained Neyman two-phase stratified pilot design and a sequential forward Horvitz-Thompson conditional log-likelihood gain estimator (\( \hat{G}_{m \mid \mathcal{S}} \)) with two-phase variance (VI + VII) and Holm lower-confidence-bound stopping. Across six benchmarks (N = 30,000 to 1,000,000; M = 15-26 native channels; 120 splits), a 15% Neyman pilot cuts discovery accesses by 85%, retains 98.3% of full-cohort Stage-2 AUPRC (95.5% of lift over Xbase; pooled \( \Delta\text{AUPRC} = -0.0059 \), 95% CI [-0.0089, -0.0029]) while matching or beating full-cohort Net Benefit on 4/6 cohorts, and records 0.0% false selection of pure-noise nulls, duplicate Stage-2 twins, and echoes across 120 stress runs (M = 25-36). Second, at deployment, calibration-only streaming Value-of-Information (VOI) routing outperforms top-risk querying in Net Benefit, while pairing VOI with conformal Benjamini-Hochberg selection controls false discoveries near target precision where Mondrian {1} singletons incur 60.7%-96.5% false discoveries.
